source_text: XV. Ἀναπέμψαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ τὸ ἀμὴν καὶ πληρώσαντος τὴν εὐχήν, οἱ τοῦ πυρὸς ἄνθρωποι ἐξῆψαν τὸ πῦρ. Μεγάλης δὲ ἐκλαμψάσης φλογὸς θαῦμα εἴδομεν, οἷς ἰδεῖν ἐδόθη· οἳ καὶ ἐτηρήθημεν εἰς τὸ ἀναγγεῖλαι τοῖς λοιποῖς τὰ γενόμενα. Τὸ γὰρ πῦρ καμάρας εἶδος ποιῆσαν, ὥσπερ ὀθόνη πλοίου ὑπὸ πνεύματος πληρουμένη, κύκλῳ περιετείχισεν τὸ σῶμα τοῦ μάρτυρος· καὶ ἦν μέσον οὐχ ὡς σὰρξ καιομένη, ἀλλ᾽ ὡς ἄρτος ὀπτώμενος, ἢ ὡς χρυσὸς καὶ ἄργυρος ἐν καμίνῳ πυρούμενος. Καὶ γὰρ εὐωδίας τοσαύτης ἀντελαβόμεθα, ὡς λιβανωτοῦ πνέοντος ἢ ἄλλου τινὸς τῶν τιμίων ἀρωμάτων.
pass_a_gloss: He having sent up the amen and having fulfilled the prayer, the men belonging to the fire kindled the fire. With a great flame flashing forth, we saw a wonder, we to whom to see was given; we who also were kept to announce to the rest the things that happened. For the fire, having made the form of a vault, just as a ship's sail being filled by wind, walled round in a circle the body of the martyr; and he was in the middle not as flesh being burned, but as bread being baked, or as gold and silver being heated in a furnace. For indeed of so great fragrance we laid hold, as of frankincense breathing forth or some other one of the precious spices.
pass_b_english: When he had uttered the Amen and finished his prayer, the attendants of the fire lit the fire. As a great flame blazed out, we beheld a wonder, we to whom it was granted to see it, and we were preserved to report to the rest what had happened.

For the fire, taking the shape of a vaulted arch, like a ship's sail filled out by the wind, walled the body of the martyr round about in a circle, and he was in the midst not as flesh burning but as bread baking, or as gold and silver being refined in a furnace. And we perceived so strong a fragrance, as of frankincense wafting forth or of some other of the costly spices.

choices.reason: kept alive as witnesses-destined, the book's own claim
